description: Values of Lh giving auroral and other signal losses (dB).

provenance.recommendation: ITU-R P.533-14 (08/2019), Recommendation ITU-R P.533-14, Method for the prediction of the performance of HF circuits
provenance.table: Table 2, Values of Lh giving auroral and other signal losses (dB)
provenance.pages: 15 and 16 of R-REC-P.533-14-201908-I!!PDF-E.pdf; part a) Transmission ranges less than or equal to 2 500 km begins on page 15, part b) Transmission ranges greater than 2 500 km on page 16, and the three Summer rows of part a) are carried over to page 16 under the heading TABLE 2 (end)
provenance.transcribed_from: Read row by row off the published table text of Recommendation ITU-R P.533-14, section 5.2.2. Each of the six blocks is eight geomagnetic-latitude rows by eight mid-path local-time columns, transcribed in the published order.
provenance.independent_check: Every one of the 384 values was compared, value for value, against the Lh[2][3][8][8] array literal in MedianSkywaveFieldStrengthShort.c of the pinned ITU reference build cd172be56dc04b154e5d2fa91cbaa6ecf5284305, which is an independent transcription of the same table by the recommendation's own authors. All 384 agree. That is a check on this transcription, not its source: the reference is a benchmark and is never vendored, and no value here was taken from it.
provenance.sha256_of_this_file: recorded in auroralLoss.ts as TABLE_2_SHA256 and re-derived by auroralLoss.test.ts, so an edit to this file without an edit to that constant fails the suite

rules.geomagnetic_pole: Section 5.2.2, the definition of Lh: "Each value is evaluated in terms of the geomagnetic latitude Gn (N or S of equator) and local time t for an Earth-centred dipole with pole at 78.5 degrees N, 68.2 degrees W: mean values for the control points of Table 1d) are taken."
rules.seasons: Section 5.2.2: "In the Northern Hemisphere, winter is taken as December-February, equinox as March-May and September-November and summer as June-August. In the Southern Hemisphere, the months for winter and summer are interchanged."
rules.local_time: The table's own column heading is "Mid-path local time, t", so the time is the local time at the path mid-point and is the same for every control point the mean is taken over.
rules.distance_regimes: The two parts of the table are headed "a) Transmission ranges less than or equal to 2 500 km" and "b) Transmission ranges greater than 2 500 km". The recommendation does not define "transmission range"; see auroralLoss.ts deviation 1 for the reading and for the alternative.

local_time_band_note: Each band is half-open, from_hours <= t < to_hours. The published bands are 01-04, 04-07, 07-10, 10-13, 13-16, 16-19, 19-22 and "22 <= t < 01"; the last wraps midnight and is written here as 22 to 25 so that a reader of the asset cannot mistake it for an empty interval. auroralLoss.ts maps t < 1 into it, which is the same set of hours.
geomagnetic_latitude_band_note: Each band is from_deg <= |Gn| < to_deg, with the first unbounded above ("77.5 degrees <= Gn") and nothing below 42.5 degrees, where Lh is zero.
